questions.prompt: Some families hesitate to vaccinate their children because of rumours. As a health volunteer, how would you respond, using science?
questions.modelAnswer: Listen to their worries respectfully. Explain that a vaccine contains a weakened, killed or harmless part of a germ, which cannot cause the full disease but trains memory cells so the child is protected. Share evidence: vaccines ended smallpox and made India polio-free, and serious side effects are very rare compared with the dangers of diseases like measles. Explain that vaccinating also protects babies and others who can't be vaccinated. Point them to their local health centre and doctors for trusted information.
rubric: Accurate explanation of how vaccines work
